title: Choose Reliable Orchestration Patterns
summary: Match deterministic workflows, model-directed routing, manager patterns, parallel work, and review loops to the uncertainty and control needs of a task.
objectives: Choose between direct execution, deterministic workflow, manager, handoff, parallel, and evaluator patterns.
Keep routing, budgets, shared state, and terminal conditions observable.
Use concurrency only for independent work and reconcile partial failure deterministically.
Distinguish portable orchestration concepts from provider-specific framework features.

sections.title: Use the simplest control structure that fits the uncertainty
paragraphs: A direct pattern performs one bounded operation and validates its result. It has the fewest boundaries, so begin there when one operation can complete the task. Use a sequential pattern when later work depends on earlier evidence. The local lab demonstrates both without calling a hosted model: trusted deterministic fixtures stand in for bounded workers.

Add conditional routing only when the input determines which specialist is needed. In the lab, the classifier returns exactly one value from a trusted map. A high-risk input selects specialistWorker, a low-risk input selects directWorker, and the unselected branch is marked skipped rather than executed. Missing or unknown routes fail closed before either worker or approval.

Write down why every boundary exists. Specialization should reduce prompt conflict, permission breadth, or evaluation ambiguity enough to justify added latency, state transfer, budget use, and failure modes. More agents create more boundaries; they do not automatically create better work.
sections.callout: Choose among seven executable shapes: direct, sequential, conditional router, manager, handoff and return, parallel join, and bounded evaluator-reviser loop.

sections.title: Keep known control flow in code
paragraphs: Sequential workflows encode ordered dependencies. The lab runs draft, then validate, then parent approval. A conditional router validates one classifier value against a closed route map, dispatches only the selected worker, records the other worker as skipped, and requires current selected evidence at the join.

The evaluator-reviser pattern is also deterministic at the graph level. An evaluator reports approval, exact unmet criteria, feedback, and artifact revision. If criteria remain unmet, a reviser changes the artifact and the evaluator runs again. The loop stops on explicit approval with no unmet criteria, a revision cap, budget exhaustion, or deadline. A revision cannot approve itself, and cap exhaustion escalates.

Google ADK documents sequential, loop, and parallel workflow agents. Anthropic describes routing and evaluator-optimizer workflows. These framework examples support a portable rule: application code owns allowed edges, contracts, limits, and terminal states while uncertain work remains inside bounded nodes.

code.label: Seven governed graph shapes
code.code:
direct:       parent action -> validate terminal result
sequential:   draft -> validate -> parent approval
router:       classify -> exactly one trusted worker -> join
manager:      parent -> specialist tool -> parent synthesis
handoff:      parent transfer -> specialist -> explicit return
parallel:     {research || review || validate} -> required join
evaluator:    evaluate -> revise -> evaluate, bounded by criteria and cap

sections.title: Decide who retains control
paragraphs: In a manager pattern, the parent remains the control owner. It invokes a specialist as a tool, receives typed evidence, applies shared guardrails, and owns synthesis and approval. The lab's research worker cannot approve; only the parent has approval authority. This centralizes control but can make the manager a bottleneck.

In a handoff pattern, active ownership changes under an explicit trusted contract. The lab permits a transfer only from parent to security-specialist with the declared acceptance contract. The specialist must then return ownership to parent under a separate return contract before approval. A result that merely claims to be a handoff is not an identity credential.

Use a manager when central synthesis and continuing parent control are required. Use a handoff when a specialist must become active under narrower instructions. In either case preserve user intent, trusted facts, tenant, permissions, unresolved questions, completed effects, budget, trace continuity, and return conditions.

sections.title: Parallelize independence, then make the join explicit
paragraphs: Parallel execution is appropriate only for independent work. In the lab, research, review, and validation use the same input snapshot but do not depend on one another or mutate shared state. Their promises start before earlier branches settle, so tests observe actual overlap and out-of-order completion rather than a parallel-looking label.

The parent still requires successful current-revision evidence from research, review, and validation. If a required branch fails, sibling completion cannot authorize approval. Late completion after a terminal decision is ignored. Optional work cannot replace a missing required dependency, and evidence is joined by dependency ID rather than completion order.

The learner exercise contains one causal edit: remove the false review-to-research dependency while keeping the parent's three required dependencies. This permits review to overlap research without weakening the join, authority, contracts, tenant checks, revision checks, timeouts, or failure behavior.

sections.title: Trace the graph and bound every edge
paragraphs: Record a run ID, parent and child span, active owner, route reason, input and output contract versions, fixture or tool calls, accepted effects, budget reservations, retries, artifact revision, and terminal state. Keep secrets and unnecessary personal data out of telemetry while retaining governed references or safe hashes.

Every node in the lab declares its tenant, role, principal, allowed actions, contracts, reservation, timeout, and attempt cap. Tests reject unknown dependencies, cycles, multiple finals, stale evidence, contract mismatches, forged approval, spoofed handoffs, conflicting writes, unsafe routes, budget exhaustion, timeouts, and final nodes that do not depend on all required work.

Run the lab locally from its directory with Node.js 22 or later. It uses deterministic fixtures, fictional budget units, and no provider or model execution. Use npm run demo for seven demonstrations, npm run trace for event evidence, npm run learner:test for the edited learner graph, and npm test for the complete suite.

activity.title: Design and simulate an orchestration graph
instructions: Open a terminal and change to training/reliable-agent-workflows/orchestration-patterns/lab.
Confirm that node --version reports Node.js 22 or later.
Run npm run regression. This executes only test/executor.test.mjs and should pass 23 tests before you edit the learner file. This establishes the unchanged regression baseline.

Run npm run learner:test. It should intentionally fail because the starting learner graph has the false dependency review -> research. This failure demonstrates that the dedicated test evaluates the editable graph.

Open src/learner.mjs. In the review node, remove only 'research' from its dependsOn array, changing it to []. Do not change the parent node or any test, fixture, delay, label, assertion, or security rule.
Save src/learner.mjs and run npm run learner:test. It should pass. The assessment should report pass=true, independent=true, and requiredJoin=true.
Run npm test. It combines the executor regression suite and the repaired learner test, and should pass 24 tests.
Run npm run learner and read the feedback. Explain that removing the false edge permits overlap among research, review, and validation while the parent still requires all three results.

Run npm run demo and npm run trace. Compare the local output with the README. These commands use deterministic local fixtures, make no remote or model run, and do not establish production performance or external-effect rollback.
If you want to inspect the reference, run npm run solution only after attempting the edit. The reference is a solution aid, not evidence that your editable learner graph was repaired.
evidence: A pattern decision record and versioned orchestration graph with explicit contracts on every edge.
Six trace records showing routes, budgets, failures, joins, and deterministic terminal states.
Terminal output showing the learner assessment passes, all three independent branches start before the join, the required join remains true, and the complete test suite passes.

Consider two branches that both edit the same policy document. Different models perform the edits, and each branch is individually fast. Should they run in parallel by default? Write down your answer and the state property that supports it. Then identify one safe redesign: serialize the writes, partition the document into nonoverlapping owned regions, or have both branches return read-only proposals for a deterministic reconciliation step.

Checkpoint. A support coordinator asks a security specialist for an analysis, receives the typed report, and remains responsible for the final customer response. Is this a manager or a handoff? Choose manager because active control never left the coordinator. Now change one fact: the specialist becomes the active owner and communicates through a narrower security workflow until an explicit return condition. That is a handoff. Your answer should depend on control ownership, not on whether two workers exist.

When ready, begin the five-question knowledge check. Question one asks you to choose deterministic sequencing for fixed ordered work. Question two checks whether you understand that a manager retains synthesis control. Questions three and four test independence and explicit join policy. Question five asks why route reasons and contract versions belong in traces. Use the executable patterns as your mental model: one bounded operation, ordered dependencies, one selected route, retained manager control, trusted transfer and return, overlapping independent branches with a required join, and measurable revision under a hard bound.
A decision funnel begins with direct execution and adds structures only when dependencies or uncertainty require them.

questions.prompt: A process has fixed ordered steps and no semantic routing decision. What is the best starting pattern?
questions.explanation: Known control flow is easier to test and govern in deterministic code.

questions.prompt: When is a manager pattern preferable to a handoff?
choices: When a central agent must combine specialist results and own the final response
When every specialist needs administrator access
questions.explanation: The manager retains control and can centralize synthesis and shared guardrails.

questions.prompt: Two branches both edit the same document. Should they run in parallel by default?
choices: Yes, because all parallelism is faster
Yes, if they use different models
No, shared mutation requires coordination or serialization
Only if neither has a budget
questions.explanation: Parallel branches should be independent or use explicit concurrency control.

questions.prompt: What must a parallel join define?
choices: Required results, timeouts, conflicts, cancellation, and partial failure
questions.explanation: Join policy determines whether concurrent work produces a predictable system outcome.

questions.prompt: Why record a route reason and contract version on each edge?
choices: To reconstruct why control moved and which interface governed the transfer
questions.explanation: Traceable routing and versioned contracts make failures reproducible and auditable.
